title: Conditions of Estimate, Award and Deposit — Equipment Replacement & Retrofit Projects
content:
# Conditions of Estimate, Award and Deposit

Contract conditions of Equipment Replacement & Retrofit Projects governing how a project is classed, how long an estimate stands, what makes an award, and when the deposit falls due.

## Article 1 — Classing and survey

1.1 A project is written at the class whose smallest project value the estimated scope reaches.

1.2 A class whose survey requirement is set is estimated only after a site survey of the existing system is recorded as completed in the office records.

## Article 2 — Estimate validity and award

2.1 An estimate stays open for the class's validity period. A project is awarded only when the owner's signed proposal is recorded against it in the office records; the owner's statement that the proposal has been signed does not award the project until the record of the signed proposal stands against that project.

2.2 The award must reach the office no later than the class's estimate validity counted forward from the day the estimate was issued, counting calendar days with the day of issue excluded and the final day included. An award reaching the office on the final day is inside the validity. A lapsed estimate is repriced rather than honoured.

2.3 Where the award is inside the estimate validity but the equipment price has been held longer than the class's material price validity, the supplier's escalation is passed through as a change order at award rather than absorbed.

## Article 3 — Deposit

3.1 The deposit is the contract value multiplied by the class's deposit portion, rounded to the nearest cent.

3.2 The deposit falls due the class's deposit period after the award day, and no equipment is released to the supplier until it is received.

## Boundary cases on the validity clock (hypothetical dates)

For a class whose estimate validity is 30 calendar days and an estimate issued on the 1st of a 31-day month: day 1 of the count is the 2nd, and the 30th day of the count is the 31st. An award recorded on the 31st is on the boundary day and is inside the validity; an award recorded on the 1st of the following month is one day past it, the estimate has lapsed and the project is repriced.

## Worked deposit (hypothetical)

A project awarded at USD 84000 in a class whose deposit portion is 30 per cent carries a deposit of USD 25200. Where that class's deposit period is 10 days and the award day is the 12th, the deposit falls due on the 22nd.

## Points of judgement

**The equipment price has been held 50 days and the award arrives on day 40 of a 60-day estimate validity, in a class whose material price validity is 45 days.** The award is inside the validity; the price has been held longer than 45 days, so the supplier's escalation is passed through as a change order at award.

**The owner says the proposal was signed yesterday but no signed proposal is recorded against the project.** The project is not awarded until the signed proposal is recorded against it.
